title: Example 14-10: Elements of Single-Frame Cartoon

illustrates.quote: Single-Frame Cartoon. Dialogue is frequently not included in a single-frame cartoon. Include sufficient information in a scene setting to convey the intent of the cartoon. a. Describe the scene setting in a transcriber’s note using 7-5 margins. b. Use 7-5 margins for the caption to the cartoon.

print.notes: There is genuinely NO print original for this example (confirmed directly against the page image, compare-gold-14/pages/page-393.png: the box under the 'Example 14-10' heading contains only the braille cells themselves, a generic labelled TEMPLATE illustrating 14.10.2/14.10.3a/14.10.4b's own structure, not a real cartoon) — per this task's brief, print.blocks is REBUILT here from the given braille (louis.backTranslate, cross-checked word-by-word by hand against the BRF ASCII) rather than left empty, so buildModel14 has something to forward-translate and this file still functions as a coverage/limitation probe. The given braille's own partial enclosure — only the single label word ('Cartoon' / 'Caption') is wrapped in transcriber's-note indicators, with the rest of that same 7-5 line ('title, artist's name, date and copyright remain' / 'Caption text') left OUTSIDE the enclosure at the identical margin — cannot be expressed in this schema at all (see resolution).
print.printFeatures: No print image exists for this example; braille-only layout skeleton.
print.transcriberNote:
Cartoon title, artist's name, date and copyright remain

braille.notes: 7-5 margins throughout (14.10.2/14.10.4a/14.10.4b); only the bracketed label word of each of the three lines/paragraphs ('Cartoon', 'Scene setting describing the cartoon' — here the WHOLE phrase is the label, 'Caption') is wrapped in transcriber's-note indicators (@.< @.>); the rest of the first and third lines continues as ordinary text at the same 7-5 margin, outside the enclosure.

uncertain: Whether 'Scene setting describing the cartoon' is meant as a label (like 'Cartoon'/'Caption') or as the FULL worked wording of a scene-setting note is not fully resolvable from a generic template with no real cartoon behind it; the given braille encloses the entire phrase, which reads naturally either way.
resolution: A/B agreed this example has no print side at all (both left print.blocks empty and recorded the same observation in their own summary.md 'Issues noted' list) and agreed on braille (byte-for-byte). Per this task's brief ('if the book shows none, rebuild the print from the braille and say so'), print.blocks was rebuilt here from the given braille via back-translation, as three 'note' blocks approximating the source's own three 7-5-margin lines. This is a KNOWN, expected approximation, not a byte-for-byte reconstruction: Emboss's 'note' block type always wraps its ENTIRE text in transcriber's-note indicators (formatTranscriberNote, document.mjs:819-826) with no mechanism to enclose only PART of a 7-5-margin line while the rest continues as plain text at the same margin (a new, third gap this reconciliation's forward-translation testing found — F-241, standards-findings.md); forward-translating the three note blocks above over-encloses the label's own trailing plain text on lines 1 and 3 (confirmed: probe output '@.<,C>TOON TITLE1 ...DATE & COPY"R REMA9@.>' vs the given braille's own '@.<,c>toon@.> title1 ... date & copy"r 9=ma;n', enclosure closed after just the label). EXPECTED MISMATCH (not-representable), recorded for completeness rather than left out of the corpus (see differences.md). Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
